free_tier.stated: Batch 1 recorded the Open Plan at 10 minutes of QPU runtime per 28-day rolling window. IBM's documentation confirms it and adds a time box and a constraint batch 1 did not carry, quoted: 'Run your quantum circuits on the world's leading QPUs for free (up to 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window)' and 'Open Plan instances can only be created in the us-east region'. The promotion is quoted: 'As of 16 March 2026, active Open Plan users can opt in to an additional 180 minutes over the next 12 months', and the blog states the precondition: 'Use 20 minutes of runtime within any 12-month period' and that the plan 'reverts back to 10 minutes/month once 12-month period ends'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: A 10-minute-a-month QPU allowance composes with a simulator on a free CPU runner, because most of the work in a variational loop can be done on a simulator and only the final evaluation needs the hardware.

limits.value: The allowance is 10 minutes in 28 days and every circuit execution plus its transpile and queue overhead spends it, so a single variational loop exhausts a month, and the 180-minute promotion cannot be reached in under two months because it requires 20 minutes of prior runtime.

The failure is the price beyond the line: one user cites USD 96 a minute on the pay-as-you-go meter, so an overrun is not a soft stop and the 10-minute window has to be watched rather than delegated.
